name: Kaduna
summary_text: Kaduna operates Sharia criminal law as one of the twelve northern states where parallel Sharia courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases. The Sharia Penal Code criminalises same-sex sexual acts between men and women for Muslims, extending beyond the federal SSMPA's coverage; per the UK country-of-origin note the maximum penalty for men's 'sodomy' is death across all twelve states, with the statutory schemes differing in detail state by state. No trans-specific incident or documented Hisbah enforcement appears for Kaduna in this dossier. Score 0.024 below the national 0.08, in the generic-Sharia tier (with Borno, Gombe, Jigawa, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger). Above Kano (0.03), whose Sharia Penal Code was the first of the wave and whose Hisbah force is the most active; above Yobe (0.04), where Hisbah is named. Below the national 0.08 purely because the parallel criminal jurisdiction exists on statute and is operational.

sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch report (2004) on the extension of Sharia to criminal law in Nigeria: Zamfara's governor was first, introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999 (in force 27 January 2000), and by 2002 twelve northern states had adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation - to date the only states where Sharia courts have jurisdiction to try criminal cases.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying USCIRF study of Sharia criminal-law implementation covers Kano, Sokoto and Zamfara using 173 cases from 2017, confirming operational Sharia-court function in Zamfara.
